To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
feature selection based solely on labeled documents is ineffective but feature selection based on human relevance feedback is effective.

(1) human feedback on features can be obtained much faster than document feedback, and (2) the performance of active learning algorithms can be significantly improved if feature selection is based on human feedback

(1) human feature feedback can significantly improve active learning, (2) human feature labeling is much less time-consuming than human document labeling, and (3) feature reweighting is a promising approach for active learning that can be further explored.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of identifying the most informative documents and features in an active learning setting, where we can query an oracle to obtain the labels.
how to improve the performance of active learning algorithms by incorporating feature selection and human input.
the following questions: 1. How does human feedback on features affect active learning? 2. How does feature selection affect active learning?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
human feedback on features can improve active learning performance by about 15-25% over standard active learning and that the time taken to do so is about 1/5 of that taken for document labeling.

the combination of feature selection and active learning has the potential for significant performance improvements, but the performance of feature selection is very sensitive to the choice of the feature selection algorithm and the quality of the human feedback.
the feature reweighting approach, which we propose and evaluate in this paper, can significantly improve the performance of active learning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the most important features are often the most difficult to identify, but that they are also the most important to identify.
the combination of feature reweighting and human feedback on feature importance can be a very effective strategy for improving classification performance.
feature selection and active learning are complimentary and can be combined to achieve the best of both worlds.
The main takeaway from our work is that
feature selection can significantly improve the efficiency of active learning, especially when we can leverage human feedback to select relevant features.

the combination of feature selection and selective sampling can significantly accelerate active learning, and that the combination of selective sampling and human feedback can improve classification performance.
feature selection is a promising avenue for improving the performance of active learning algorithms.
